name: IPTV Checker
description: A Dispatcharr Plugin that goes through a playlist to check IPTV channels
author: PiratesIRC

fields.label: 📥 Group Selection
fields.description: Which Dispatcharr channel groups get checked, and whether backup streams are checked as well as the first one. An empty list means every group in both modes. Take care with a typo: in include mode a pattern that matches nothing selects nothing, but in exclude mode it excludes nothing, so the run covers every group and every one of them becomes eligible for the scheduled rename, move and delete. Press Validate Settings to see how many groups are in scope before running anything.

fields.label: 📁 Channel Groups (comma-separated)
fields.help_text: The channel groups this plugin should act on. Leave empty for all groups. Wildcards are supported: * matches any characters, ? matches one, and [abc] matches a character from the set. Matching is case-sensitive. How this list is read depends on the Channel Groups Mode setting directly below. A group name or pattern that matches nothing is reported as an error by Validate Settings in both modes, because a typo in exclude mode would check the group you meant to skip.

fields.label: 🔀 Channel Groups Mode

options.label: Check only the groups listed above
Check all groups except those listed above

fields.help_text: Decides whether the Channel Groups list names the groups to check or the groups to skip. Use the second option when a group should be left alone, for example pay-per-view or event channels. The second option also means a group you create later is checked automatically, whereas listing groups to check means a new group is skipped until you add it. Leaving the Channel Groups box empty checks every group either way. This replaces the separate Group(s) to Check and Group(s) to EXCLUDE settings; if you had values in those, they are read automatically until you save this one.

fields.label: 🔄 Check Alternative Streams
fields.help_text: Check all alternative/backup streams for each channel in addition to the primary stream. This will significantly increase check time.

fields.label: 👁️ Only Check Visible Channels
fields.help_text: Only check channels that are enabled (visible) in at least one Channel Profile. Channels disabled in every profile (or not assigned to any profile) are skipped. Useful for ignoring hidden/archived channels.

fields.label: 🔍 Check Behavior
fields.description: Timeouts, retries, concurrency, and cooldown. Keep worker count below your provider's concurrent-connection limit.

fields.label: ⏱️ Connection Timeout (seconds)
fields.help_text: Network connection timeout. Use for detecting dead streams that refuse connections. Default: 10

fields.label: 🔍 Probe Timeout (seconds)
fields.help_text: Maximum time to wait for stream to start delivering data after connection. Increase this for streams with slow startup (5+ seconds). Default: 20

fields.label: 🔄 Dead Connection Retries
fields.help_text: Number of times to retry checking a stream if it appears to be dead. Default: 3

fields.label: ⚡ Enable Parallel Stream Checking
fields.help_text: Check multiple streams simultaneously for significantly faster processing. Recommended for large channel lists.

fields.label: 👷 Number of Parallel Workers
fields.help_text: Number of streams to check simultaneously when parallel checking is enabled. Default: 2. Higher values = faster but more resource-intensive. Keep BELOW your provider's max concurrent connection limit.

fields.label: ⏳ Per-Stream Cooldown (seconds)
fields.help_text: Cooldown each worker waits after finishing a stream check, before picking up the next. Prevents provider rate-limiting / slot-reuse errors when your account has a concurrent-connection limit. Default: 2. Retry passes use 3x this value.

fields.label: ⬛ Blank-Screen Detection
fields.description: Optionally decode a few seconds of each Alive stream with ffmpeg and mark it Dead if it is a pure blank (all-black) screen. Costs extra CPU/time per Alive stream.

fields.label: ⬛ Detect Blank-Screen Streams
fields.help_text: When ON, every stream that passes ffprobe is decoded for a few seconds with ffmpeg's blackdetect filter; pure-blank (all-black) streams are marked Dead and reported under the `Black Screen` error type so rename/move/delete actions handle them. Adds ~5-10s per Alive stream. Fail-open: if ffmpeg is missing or errors, the stream stays Alive. Very-dark-but-not-black 'no signal' slates are NOT detected.

fields.label: ⬛ Blank-Screen Sample (seconds)
fields.help_text: How many seconds of video to decode when testing for a blank screen. Longer = more reliable but slower. Default: 6

fields.label: ⬛ Continuous Blank Required (seconds)
fields.help_text: Minimum continuous run of blank (all-black) video (within the sample) required to flag a stream as blank. Should be a few seconds less than the sample to allow for connection/keyframe latency. Default: 3

fields.label: ⬛ Blank-Screen ffmpeg Timeout (seconds)
fields.help_text: Hard wall-clock cap on the ffmpeg blank-screen decode (connection + sampling). If exceeded, the stream is left Alive. Default: 20

fields.label: 📄 Placeholder-File Detection
fields.description: A continuous live stream reports no fixed duration. A stream that DOES report one is serving a finite file, which providers use as a dead-channel placeholder. Costs nothing extra: the duration is already read during the normal ffprobe check.

fields.label: 📄 Detect Placeholder-File Streams
fields.help_text: When ON, any stream reporting a fixed container duration is marked Dead under the `Placeholder File` error type, so the dead-channel rename/move/delete actions handle it. Adds no probe time. Measured against a full sweep of 156 provider channels: all 138 healthy channels reported no duration, while all 19 that did were serving a placeholder file. The duration and container bitrate are recorded in the CSV for every stream even when this is OFF, so you can check the evidence before turning it on. Leave OFF if any channel here is fed by a finite file you want to keep.

fields.label: 🧊 Frozen-Video Detection
fields.description: Detects a stream whose picture has stopped moving but is not blank. A still frame passes ffprobe and is not black, so blank-screen detection cannot see it. Shares the same single ffmpeg decode pass as blank-screen and silent-audio detection, so enabling several of them costs one provider connection, not one each.

fields.label: 🧊 Detect Frozen-Video Streams
fields.help_text: When ON, the decoded sample is checked for a continuous run of identical frames and matching streams are marked Dead under the `Frozen Video` error type, so the dead-channel rename/move/delete actions handle them. A blank screen is also a still picture, so blank-screen detection takes precedence when both are ON and both fire. Uses the Blank-Screen Sample length below for how much video to decode. Fail-open: if ffmpeg is missing or errors, the stream stays Alive.

fields.label: 🧊 Frozen-Video Minimum (seconds)
fields.help_text: How many continuous seconds the picture must stay identical before the stream counts as frozen. Automatically reduced to fit inside the sample length, because a value at or above the sample can never be reached and would leave the setting looking active while never firing. Default: 4

fields.label: 🔇 Silent-Audio Detection
fields.description: Detects a stream carrying a healthy audio track that is completely silent. This is different from a stream with no audio track at all, which is not flagged. Shares the same ffmpeg decode pass as the two detectors above.

fields.label: 🔇 Detect Silent-Audio Streams
fields.help_text: When ON, the mean volume of the decoded sample is measured and streams at or below the threshold are marked Dead under the `Silent Audio` error type. Skipped entirely for streams with no audio track, which cannot be silent. Fail-open: if the volume cannot be measured the stream stays Alive, because no measurement is not evidence of silence. Note this marks a stream Dead even though its video is fine, so the dead-channel delete action would remove a channel that still has a picture.

fields.label: 🔇 Silence Threshold (dBFS)
fields.help_text: Mean volume at or below this level counts as silence. Must be negative. Measured basis: digitally silent audio reports -91.0 dB, while the quietest real channel measured reported -44.4 dB, so the default of -70 sits roughly midway with about 25 dB of margin on each side. Raise it toward -50 to catch very quiet channels, at the risk of flagging quiet film soundtracks. Default: -70

fields.label: 🏷️ Post-Check Actions
fields.description: What to do with channels once a check has finished: rename them, move them to another group, or restore ones that recovered. The five sections below set the tags and destination groups only. Nothing is applied until you press the matching action, or switch it on for scheduled runs further down the form.

fields.label: ✏️ Dead Channel Handling
fields.description: How to rename and relocate a channel when every one of its streams failed to play. These settings only describe the tag and the destination; nothing is applied until you press the matching action or switch it on for scheduled runs further down the form.

fields.label: 💀 Dead Channel Rename Format
fields.help_text: Format for renaming dead channels. Use {name} as placeholder for the original channel name. Examples: '[DEAD] {name}', '{name} [DEAD]', '[X] {name} [DEAD]'

fields.label: ⚰️ Move Dead Channels to Group
fields.help_text: Enter the name for the group to move dead channels into.

fields.label: ⬛ Blank-Screen Handling
fields.description: How to rename and relocate channels detected as a pure blank (all-black) screen. Requires 'Detect Blank-Screen Streams' to be ON. These channels are handled separately from [DEAD] channels (excluded from the Dead rename/move actions).

fields.label: ⬛ Blank-Screen Channel Rename Format
fields.help_text: Format for renaming blank-screen channels. Use {name} as the placeholder. Blank-screen channels are excluded from the Dead rename/move actions so they are not double-tagged.

fields.label: ⬛ Move Blank-Screen Channels to Group
fields.help_text: Enter the name for the group to move blank-screen channels into.

fields.label: 🐌 Low Framerate Handling
fields.description: How to rename and relocate channels whose streams deliver below 24 fps.

fields.label: 🐌 Low Framerate Rename Format - Below 24fps
fields.help_text: Format for renaming low framerate channels. Use {name} as placeholder for the original channel name.

fields.label: 📁 Move Low Framerate Channels to Group
fields.help_text: Enter the name for the group to move low framerate channels into.

fields.label: 🎬 Format Suffixes
fields.description: Append a resolution tag (e.g. [HD], [FHD]) to channel names based on probed format.

fields.label: 🎬 Add Video Format Suffixes - [UHD], [FHD], [HD], [SD], [Unknown]
fields.help_text: A comma-separated list of formats to add as a suffix (e.g., [HD]) to channel names.

fields.label: ♻️ Restore Recovered Channels
fields.description: Channels that come back Alive can be auto-cleaned: plugin name tags ([DEAD]/[Slow]/[Blank]/quality) are stripped and the channel is moved back to the original group captured when it was first moved. Use the 'Restore Recovered Channels' action or the scheduler toggle. NOTE: a channel parked in a managed group (Graveyard / Slow / blank-screen) is only re-checked (and thus restorable) if your scan scope includes that group.

fields.label: ⏰ Scheduling & Automation
fields.description: When the plugin runs on its own, and how long each run is allowed to last. Times use the timezone Dispatcharr is configured with, not this machine's clock. Separate several schedules with a semicolon or a newline, never a comma, because a comma is also legal inside a cron field where it lists values. Which actions a scheduled run then applies is set in the three sections below this one.

fields.label: ⏰ Scheduled Check Times (Cron Format)
fields.help_text: One or more cron expressions. Format: 'minute hour day month weekday' (weekday: 0=Sunday, 6=Saturday). Examples: '0 4 * * *' (daily at 4 AM), '0 0,8,16 * * *' (daily at midnight, 8 AM and 4 PM), '0 3 * * 0' (Sundays at 3 AM), '0 2 */2 * *' (every 2 days at 2 AM). To run several different expressions, separate them with a semicolon, for example '0 4 * * * ; 0 3 1 * *'. Leave blank to disable scheduling. 💾 After editing this field, click "💾 Save Schedule" below to apply the new schedule.

fields.label: 🪟 Use Windowed Schedule (run only during a time window)
fields.help_text: When on, your Scheduled Times above mark the START of a run window. The check runs until the configured end-time / duration, then halts cleanly between streams. The next time the window opens it RESUMES from the same point (channels already checked are skipped). Group selection, alternative-stream and visible-only settings are read fresh at each window fire.

fields.label: 🛑 Window End Mode
fields.help_text: Choose how the window ends. Duration counts forward from the cron-fire time. Time mode supports past-midnight wrap (e.g. start 22:00, end 02:00).

fields.label: ⏳ Window Duration (hours)
fields.help_text: Used when Window End Mode = duration. Decimals allowed (e.g. 3.5). Default: 4 hours.

fields.label: 🕓 Window End Time (HH:MM, scheduler timezone)
fields.help_text: Used when Window End Mode = time. 24-hour format in Dispatcharr's timezone. If earlier than the start time, the window is treated as wrapping past midnight.

fields.label: ⚙️ Auto-run After Scheduled Checks
fields.description: What a scheduled check leaves behind. The CSV export always runs and is not optional, because it is the record of what was probed when a destructive action follows. A window that closes part way through the list still writes its CSV and still sends the report, and defers only the channel changes to the window that finishes the list. A run stopped from outside, which happens when the Dispatcharr Plugins page is opened during a check, writes its CSV and sends nothing else.

fields.label: 📧 Email Report After Scheduled Check
fields.help_text: When ON, each scheduled check builds the HTML report and queues it for delivery by email through Newsflasharr. Runs beside the CSV export and on the same terms, so a window that closes part way through the channel list still leaves a report. Requires the Newsflasharr plugin, its SMTP settings, and a routing rule matching source iptv_checker and event usage_report with channel smtp. Without that rule the report is delivered somewhere else, so the plugin checks for it first and refuses rather than reporting a success you cannot verify.

fields.label: 🧹 Delete CSV Exports Older Than (Days)
fields.help_text: Housekeeping for the CSV files this plugin writes to /data/exports/. After each export, its own exports older than this many days are deleted. 0 keeps every file, which is the default, so nothing is removed unless you ask for it. The file just written is never deleted, and at least one file always survives. Only files named iptv_checker_results_*.csv are touched, because that directory is shared with other plugins.

fields.label: 🔄 Auto-run: Reversible Channel Changes
fields.description: Which renaming and moving a scheduled check applies on its own. Restore Recovered Channels undoes the renames and the moves, because each move records the group the channel came from. It does NOT strip the video format suffix, which is applied to channels that play rather than to ones that failed. A channel is judged by all of its streams, so one that still plays on a backup is never renamed or moved however many of its other streams failed.

fields.label: ♻️ Restore Recovered Channels After Scheduled Checks
fields.help_text: After each scheduled check, channels that are Alive again but were previously marked by this plugin have their name tags ([DEAD]/[Slow]/[Blank]/quality) stripped and are moved back to their original group. Runs first, before re-marking. NOTE: a channel parked in a managed group (Graveyard / Slow / blank-screen) is only re-checked (and thus restorable) if your scan scope includes that group.

fields.label: 💀 Rename Dead Channels After Scheduled Checks
fields.help_text: Automatically rename dead channels after scheduled checks complete.

fields.label: ⬛ Rename Blank-Screen Channels After Scheduled Checks
fields.help_text: Automatically rename blank-screen channels after scheduled checks complete. Requires 'Detect Blank-Screen Streams' to be ON.

fields.label: 🐌 Rename Low Framerate Channels After Scheduled Checks
fields.help_text: Automatically rename low framerate channels after scheduled checks complete.

fields.label: 🎬 Add Video Format Suffix After Scheduled Checks
fields.help_text: Automatically add video format suffixes to channels after scheduled checks complete.

fields.label: ⚰️ Move Dead Channels After Scheduled Checks
fields.help_text: Automatically move dead channels to the configured group after scheduled checks complete.

fields.label: ⬛ Move Blank-Screen Channels After Scheduled Checks
fields.help_text: Automatically move blank-screen channels to the configured group after scheduled checks complete.

fields.label: 📁 Move Low Framerate Channels After Scheduled Checks
fields.help_text: Automatically move low framerate channels to the configured group after scheduled checks complete.

fields.label: 🗑 Auto-run: Deletion, Which Cannot Be Undone
fields.description: The only automatic action that removes something. Deleting needs both the toggle below and the confirmation word typed beside it, and it acts only on channels where every stream failed to play and none was merely skipped. A channel whose streams were rate limited, or which carries audio only, has not been shown to be broken and is never deleted.

fields.label: 🗑️ Delete Dead Channels After Scheduled Checks
fields.help_text: WARNING: This will PERMANENTLY DELETE dead channels from Dispatcharr after scheduled checks. This action is IRREVERSIBLE. Deleted channels and their stream associations cannot be recovered. The 'Auto-Delete Confirmation' field must also contain the word DELETE for this to take effect.

fields.label: ⚠️ Auto-Delete Confirmation (type DELETE to enable)
fields.help_text: SAFETY GATE: You must type the word DELETE (all caps) in this field to enable auto-deletion. This prevents accidental deletion of channels. If this field does not contain exactly DELETE, the delete function will refuse to run even if the toggle is enabled.

fields.label: ⚙️ Advanced
fields.description: Paths and low-level overrides. Change only if your environment differs from the Dispatcharr defaults.

fields.label: 🔍 FFprobe Analysis Flags
fields.help_text: Comma-separated ffprobe flags for stream analysis. Options: -show_streams (basic validation), -show_packets (per-packet data; required for video bitrate calculation on live MPEG-TS streams), -loglevel error (errors only). Default: -show_streams,-show_packets,-loglevel error. Note: do not add -show_frames. When both -show_frames and -show_packets are passed, ffprobe returns a combined packets_and_frames array instead of separate packets[], which stops the bitrate fallback running.

fields.label: ⏱️ FFprobe Analysis Duration (seconds)
fields.help_text: Duration to analyze stream when using -show_frames or -show_packets. Longer duration = more accurate bitrate/GOP analysis but slower checks. Probes that capture fewer than 30 video packets leave video_bitrate unset, so 8s gives slow-start streams enough room to clear the threshold. Default: 8 seconds

fields.label: ⏼ Streamlink-Only Hosts (skip ffprobe)
fields.help_text: Comma-separated host suffixes that ffprobe cannot validate (served via Streamlink). Streams on these hosts are marked 'Skipped' instead of 'Dead' so rename/move/delete actions leave them alone. Use full domains (e.g. 'youtube.com', not 'youtube'). Leave blank to use the defaults.

fields.label: 📍 FFprobe Path
fields.help_text: Full path to the ffprobe executable. Default: /usr/local/bin/ffprobe (Dispatcharr's default location)

fields.label: 📍 FFmpeg Path
fields.help_text: Full path to the ffmpeg executable, used for blank-screen detection. Default: /usr/local/bin/ffmpeg (Dispatcharr's default location)

actions.label: ✅ Validate Settings
actions.description: Validate all plugin settings (database connectivity, groups, etc.).

actions.label: 📅 Update Schedule
actions.description: Apply the current schedule settings. If scheduled times are empty, the schedule will be cleared and scheduler will be stopped.

actions.label: 🔄 Reset Window Progress
actions.description: Clear the windowed-schedule resume state. The next window will start fresh from the full channel list instead of resuming where the last window left off.

actions.label: 🔍 Check Scheduler Status
actions.description: Display scheduler thread status and diagnostic information.

actions.label: 📥 Load Group(s)
actions.description: Load channels from the specified Dispatcharr group(s) (or all groups if blank).

actions.label: ▶️ Start Stream Check
actions.description: Start checking stream status and quality for all loaded channels.

actions.label: 📊 View Check Progress
actions.description: View the current progress and ETA of the running stream check.

actions.label: 🛑 Cancel Stream Check
actions.description: Cancel the currently running stream check.

confirm.message: Cancel the in-progress stream check? Streams already probed are kept; queued and in-flight streams are aborted (ffprobe currently running may take a few seconds to exit).

actions.label: 📋 View Last Results
actions.description: View summary of the last completed stream check.

actions.label: ✏️ Rename Dead Channels
actions.description: Rename all channels marked as Dead in the last check using the configured rename format.

confirm.message: This renames channels where every stream failed to play. Restore Recovered Channels undoes this. Continue?

actions.label: ⚰️ Move Dead Channels to Group
actions.description: Moves all channels marked as Dead in the last check to the specified group.

confirm.message: This moves channels where every stream failed to play into the configured group. Restore Recovered Channels undoes this. Continue?

actions.label: ⬛ Rename Blank-Screen Channels
actions.description: Rename all channels detected as a blank screen in the last check using the configured format.

confirm.message: This renames channels serving a blank picture on every stream. Restore Recovered Channels undoes this. Continue?

actions.label: ⬛ Move Blank-Screen Channels to Group
actions.description: Moves all channels detected as a blank screen in the last check to the specified group.

confirm.message: This moves channels serving a blank picture into the configured group. Restore Recovered Channels undoes this. Continue?

actions.label: ♻️ Restore Recovered Channels
actions.description: For channels that are Alive again but were previously marked: strip plugin name tags and move them back to their original group.

confirm.message: This will strip plugin tags from recovered channel names and move them back to their original groups. Continue?

actions.label: 🐌 Rename Low Framerate Channels
actions.description: Rename channels with streams under 30fps using the configured rename format.

confirm.message: This renames channels running below the framerate threshold. Restore Recovered Channels undoes this. Continue?

actions.label: 📁 Move Low Framerate Channels
actions.description: Moves channels with streams under 30fps to the specified group.

confirm.message: This moves channels running below the framerate threshold into the configured group. Restore Recovered Channels undoes this. Continue?

actions.label: 🎬 Add Video Format Suffix
actions.description: Adds a format suffix like [HD] or [FHD] to alive channel names.

confirm.message: This appends a quality suffix to the names of channels that play. Restore Recovered Channels does NOT strip these suffixes, because it acts only on channels this plugin marked as failing. Continue?

actions.label: 📊 View Results Table
actions.description: Display detailed results in table format. (Copy/paste into text editor for better formatting.)

actions.label: 💾 Export Results to CSV
actions.description: Export the last check results to a CSV file. Will be saved in Docker container: /data/exports/

actions.label: 📧 Email Report
actions.description: Build the HTML report from the last check and queue it for delivery by email through Newsflasharr. The report is always written to disk first, so a delivery problem never costs you the report.

actions.label: 🧹 Cleanup Orphaned Tasks
actions.description: Remove any orphaned Celery periodic tasks from old plugin versions.

actions.label: 🗑️ Clear CSV Exports
actions.description: Delete all CSV export files created by this plugin.

confirm.message: This deletes every CSV this plugin wrote to /data/exports/. Files other plugins wrote to that shared directory are not touched. Continue?

actions.label: 🗑️ Delete Dead Channels
actions.description: Permanently delete all channels marked as Dead in the last check from the database.

confirm.message: WARNING: This will PERMANENTLY DELETE dead channels from the database. This action CANNOT be undone. The 'Auto-Delete Confirmation' field must contain DELETE for this to work. Continue?
